chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ma'roof ibn Kharbouz, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are winds of Mercy and winds of Punishment. So if Allah desires to make the Punishment from the winds into Mercy, He does it. He said: And He will never make the Mercy from the wind into Punishment.
And that is because He never showed mercy to a people who obeyed Him, and their obedience to Him became an affliction upon them, except after they turned away from their obedience.

He said: Thus He acted with the people of Yunus. When they believed, Allah showed mercy to them after having ordained the Punishment for them and decreed it. Then He encompassed them with His Mercy, so He made the pre-destined Punishment for them into Mercy, and turned it away from them, although it had already descended upon them and overwhelmed them. And that was when they believed in him and pleaded humbly to Him.

He said: And as for the barren wind (Al-Aqeem), it is a wind of Punishment. It does not inseminate anything from the wombs or anything from the plants. And it is a wind that emerges from beneath the seven earths.
And no wind ever emerged from it except upon the people of Aad, when Allah was wrathful against them. So He commanded the Keepers to bring out from it a measure equal to the width of a ring.
He said: So it rebelled against the Keepers, and there emerged from it a measure equal to the nostril of a bull, being wrathful against the people of Aad.

He said: So the Keepers cried out to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from that, saying: 'Our Lord! It has rebelled against our command. We fear that it will destroy those who did not disobey You from Your creatures and the builders of Your land.'

He said: So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent Jibraeel (peace be upon him) towards it. He faced it with his two wings and returned it to its place, and said to it: 'Come out according to what you were commanded.'
He said: So it came out according to what it was commanded, and destroyed the people of Aad and those who were present with them.

key_terms.الرِّيحُ الْعَقِيمُ: The barren wind (a specific wind of punishment)
key_terms.الْخُزَّانُ: The Keepers (angels or entities controlling the winds)
key_terms.تَدَارَكَهُمْ: He encompassed them / intervened with mercy

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the winds of mercy and the winds of punishment in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine mechanics of wind as a vessel for both mercy and punishment, highlighting Allah's absolute sovereignty to convert destined chastisement into mercy, as exemplified by the people of Yunus. The narration further details the cosmological origin of the 'barren wind' (Al-Aqeem) from beneath the seven earths, describing its temporary rebellion against the angelic Keepers and its ultimate subjugation by Jibraeel to execute the destruction of the people of Aad, illustrating the precise interplay between divine command and natural forces.
